subject: Civil Engineering
title: Steel Ribs and Lattice Girders
description: A short lesson to help you apply Steel Ribs and Lattice Girders.

hook.text: In weak ground, shotcrete alone isn't enough — steel ribs provide an internal skeleton.

buildup.text: Curved steel I-beams are erected against the tunnel profile — then shotcrete encases them.

discovery.text: Lattice girders — lighter, triangulated frames — replaced heavy ribs in many applications.

twist.text: The combination works like reinforced concrete — steel handles tension, shotcrete handles compression.

climax.text: In squeezing ground — clay under high stress — ribs may need to be installed every 2 feet.

punchline.text: Steel frames give shotcrete a backbone in ground too weak to stand alone.

quiz.question: Why are steel ribs used alongside shotcrete in weak ground?
options: Steel ribs are decorative elements required by architectural standards
They provide an internal skeleton that reinforces the shotcrete where ground is too weak
Steel ribs replace the need for rock bolts in all conditions

details.summary: Steel ribs are curved I-beams or H-beams installed in tunnel sections to provide immediate heavy support in poor ground conditions. Lattice girders are lighter triangular steel frameworks that serve as reinforcement for shotcrete linings.
details.whyItMatters: Steel ribs and lattice girders provide critical structural support in weak ground where shotcrete and rock bolts alone cannot prevent tunnel deformation or collapse during construction.
takeaways: Steel ribs provide immediate heavy support in squeezing or collapsing ground
Lattice girders reinforce shotcrete and maintain layer bonding for composite action
Rib spacing typically ranges from 0.5-1.5 meters depending on ground quality

faq.question: When are steel ribs preferred over rock bolts and shotcrete alone?
faq.answer: Steel ribs are used in very poor ground conditions like fault zones, heavily fractured rock, or squeezing clay where rock bolts cannot anchor effectively and shotcrete alone lacks sufficient bending resistance. They provide immediate structural capacity before shotcrete gains strength.

faq.question: Why are lattice girders replacing traditional steel ribs in many applications?
faq.answer: Lattice girders are lighter, easier to handle, and allow shotcrete to flow through and around them, creating a composite structure. Traditional ribs create shadows where shotcrete cannot reach, leaving voids. Lattice girders provide better shotcrete integration and similar structural performance.
